newsitem.title: USA: Soyoil ends up, nearby soymeal also ends higher.
newsitem.headline: Soyoil ends up, nearby soymeal also ends higher.

text.p: Soyoil futures ended with modest gains on soybean spillover, while firm cash basis kept nearby soymeal contracts firm, traders said.
"There's not much going on in the meal market but I know that nobody wants to sell it (futures)," one trader said.
Soyoil cash markets were quiet, and most of the strength in Thursday's trade was provided by soybeans, traders said.
CBOT July soybean futures shot higher Thursday on ideas that supplies of soybeans for prompt shipment were too tight.
On Thursday, the CBOT reported deliverable soybean supplies were a very small 20,000 bushels at Toledo.
Soymeal futures were underpinned by reports that basis offers in some Illinois markets rose as much $13.00 per ton as livestock dealers bought spot supplies, traders said.
Futures volume was said to be extremely light throughout the session, traders said.
CBOT July soymeal settled up $2.60 per ton at $276.70 and other months were $1.60 lower to $0.30 higher. July soyoil ended up 0.07 cent a lb at 23.24, and other months were 0.05 to 0.14 higher.
